# iliad-101 (16.210–305) — new renderings

| Greek | `l` | `i` | avoided on purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| ἀράρῃ · ἄραρον · ἄρθεν (ἀραρίσκω, 16.212, 16.214, 16.211) | "fits together" · "were fitted together" · "were fitted together" | "fits together" · "were fitted together" · "closed up" | "builds", "joins", "locks"; ἀραρίσκω keeps "fit" (ἀραρυίας 3.331, ἀρήρει 3.338); the note says ἄρθεν is read as the passive of this verb, not of ἀείρω "lift" |
| πυκινοῖσι λίθοισι · πυκινὴν νεφέλην (16.212, 16.298) | "solid stones" · "a solid cloud" | "close-set stones" · "a dense cloud" | "thick", "shrewd" (πυκινὴ βουλή); `l` keeps the table’s "solid" (πυκινὸς δόμος, 3.202), `i` takes the English word that fits stones and cloud |
| τοῖχον (16.212, of a house) | "a wall" | "the wall" | "partition", "side" (the table’s τοῖχος of a ship is "the sides") |
| ἕνα θυμὸν ἔχοντες (16.219) | "having one heart" | "with one heart between them" | "of one mind", "united in spirit"; θυμός "heart" |
| ἀνεμοσκεπέων (χλαινάων, 16.224) | "wind-sheltering" | "to shelter from the wind" | "windproof", "weatherproof", "wind-breaking"; ἄνεμος "wind" and the root of σκέπας "shelter" |
| οὔλων ταπήτων (16.224) | "thick rugs" | "thick rugs" | "coverlets", "carpets", "woollen"; οὖλος "thick" as in the Odyssey’s χλαῖναι οὖλαι (19.225), τάπης "rug" |
| ἔνιψ’ · νίψατο (νίζω, 16.229, 16.230) | "washed" · "washed" | "washed" · "washed" | "rinsed" (turned down for ἐξαπονίζω, 19.387), "bathed", "cleansed" (kept for ἐκάθηρε, 16.228) |
| μέσῳ ἕρκεϊ (16.231) | "in the middle of the enclosure" | "in the middle of the enclosure" | "court", "yard", "fence" (the table’s ἕρκος "fence", 15.566, is a barrier; here a space is meant); the note says the Greek does not say whose |
| εἰσανιδών (οὐρανὸν εἰσανιδών, 16.232) | "looking up at" | "looking up at" | "gazing", "lifting his eyes to", "looking toward"; εἰς + ἀνά + the root of ἰδεῖν "see" |
| Δία δ’ οὐ λάθε τερπικέραυνον (16.232) | "and Zeus, delighting-in-the-thunderbolt, he did not escape" | "and he did not escape the notice of Zeus, who delights in the thunderbolt" | "Zeus was not unaware", "he did not go unseen by Zeus"; λανθάνω with the accusative of the person; τερπικέραυνος keeps the table’s "delighting-in-the-thunderbolt" / "who delights in the thunderbolt" (1.419) |
| Ζεῦ ἄνα Δωδωναῖε Πελασγικέ (16.233) | "Zeus, lord, of Dodona, Pelasgian" | "Lord Zeus of Dodona, Pelasgian" | "Dodonaean", "Pelasgic", "Zeus of the Pelasgians"; Ζεῦ ἄνα follows the table’s row (3.351), and Πελασγικός "Pelasgian" follows the shipped "Pelasgian Argos" (2.681); the note says why the god bears the name is not said |
| τηλόθι ναίων (16.233) | "dwelling far away" | "you who dwell far away" | "afar", "living remote", "who inhabit distant lands"; ναίω "dwell" as in the Odyssey table |
| Δωδώνης μεδέων δυσχειμέρου (16.234) | "ruling over Dodona, harsh-wintered" | "you who rule over Dodona of the harsh winters" | "lord of Dodona" (μεδέων is the participle, not the noun μέδων), "wintry" (reserved for χειμέριος); follows the table’s μεδέων "ruling" (Ἴδηθεν μεδέων, 3.276) and δυσχείμερος "harsh-wintered" / "of the harsh winters" (2.750) |
| Σελλοί (16.234) | "the Selli" | "the Selli" | "Helli" (the other ancient spelling); a name, as the table’s names |
| ὑποφῆται (16.235) | "interpreters" | "interpreters" | "prophets", "priests", "spokesmen", "attendants"; ὑπό + φημί "speak for", and the note says they speak for the god |
| ἀνιπτόποδες · χαμαιεῦναι (16.235) | "with unwashed feet" · "sleeping on the ground" | "with unwashed feet" · "who sleep on the ground" | "unwashed-footed", "ground-sleepers", "lying on the earth", "beggars"; ἄνιπτος "unwashed" + πούς, χαμαί "on the ground" + εὐνή "bed" |
| ἠμὲν δή ποτ’ … ἠδ’ ἔτι καὶ νῦν (16.236–238) | "both once indeed … and still, even now" | "as once … and further, even now" | "truly indeed" (the shipped English of the nearly identical 1.453, where the line begins ἦ μὲν δή); here ἠμέν answers ἠδ’, so the pair is "both … and"; 16.238 takes the published English of 1.455 unchanged |
| τῷ κῦδος ἅμα πρόες (16.241) | "therefore glory along with him send" | "so send glory with him" | "to him send glory" (τῷ as a dative); the note gives both readings. προΐημι "send forth", κῦδος "glory" |
| δίηται (μάχην ἐνοπήν τε δίηται, 16.246) | "he has driven" | "he has driven … away" | "chased off", "put to flight", "driven back"; δίεμαι/δίημι "drive away"; ἐνοπή "shouting" follows the table (3.2) |
| ἀνένευσε (ἀνανεύω with an object, 16.250, 16.252) | "he refused with a sign" | "he refused with a sign" | "signed a refusal" and "made a sign of refusal" (the table’s English for the Odyssey’s ἀνένευε, 21.129, which has no object; kept for it), "denied", "shook his head" (the Greek says the head is thrown back) |
| σόον … μάχης ἐξαπονέεσθαι (16.252) | "to come back safe from the battle" | "that he should come back from the fighting safe" | "to escape", "to return unharmed"; ἐξαπονέομαι "come back out" (ἀπονέεσθαι "go back", 12.73), σῶς "safe" |
| εἰνοδίοις (σφήκεσσιν … εἰνοδίοις, 16.260) | "wayside" | "wayside" | "of the road", "roadside", "that live in roads"; ἐν + ὁδός, the note says the Greek gives where they nest |
| ἐριδμαίνωσιν (16.260) | "provoke" | "provoke" | "enrage", "irritate", "stir to strife", "madden"; the verb is built on ἔρις "strife", and the note says the exact formation is not certain |
| ἔθοντες (16.260) | "being used to it" | "being used to it" | "being in the habit", "accustomed", "wont"; ἔθω "be used to" |
| κερτομέοντες (of boys and wasps, 16.261) | "taunting" | "teasing" | "mocking" (kept for the Odyssey’s κερτομέοντες of men, 8.153), "tormenting", "jeering"; κερτομίοις "taunting" (1.539) in `l` |
| ξυνὸν δὲ κακὸν πολέεσσι τιθεῖσι (16.262) | "and a common evil for many they set" | "and they set an evil that is common to many" | "a shared harm", "a harm to all"; ξυνός "common" as in ξυνήϊα "common goods" (1.124) |
| ἀμύνει οἷσι τέκεσσι (16.265) | "defends its own young" | "defends its own young" | "wards off … for", "protects"; "wards off" is kept for ἀμύνω with the accusative of the danger (κῆρας ἀμύνει, 4.11); τέκος "young"; οἷσι the possessive ὅς, not the relative |
| ἀγχέμαχοι θεράποντες (16.272) | "close-fighting attendants" | "his close-fighting attendants" | "squires", "servants", "henchmen"; ἀγχέμαχος "close-fighting" (Μυσῶν ἀγχεμάχων, 13.5) and θεράπων "attendant" (2.110) |
| ἐν δ’ ἔπεσον … ἀολλέες (16.276) | "fell upon … in a body" | "fell upon … in a body" | "in a mass", "crowded", "all together" (kept for ἀθρόοι); ἀολλής "in a body" |
| ὀρίνθη · ἐκίνηθεν · κινήσῃ (16.280, 16.280, 16.298) | "was stirred up" · "were moved" · "moves" | "was stirred" · "shook" · "stirs" | "was shaken" (reserved for ἐκίνηθεν), "troubled", "was moved" (reserved for the battle-lines); ὀρίνω "stir up", κινέω "move" |
| ἀπορρῖψαι (μηνιθμὸν ἀπορρῖψαι, 16.282) | "to have cast off" | "had cast off" | "thrown away", "put aside", "given up"; the aorist infinitive after ἐλπόμενοι refers to what is hoped already done; μηνιθμός "wrath" (16.62), φιλότης "friendship" |
| ἀντικρὺ κατὰ μέσσον (16.285) | "straight into the middle" | "straight into the middle" | "through the centre", "right at the middle"; ἀντικρύ "straight" as in the shipped rows (ἀντικρὺ δὲ δι’ ὤμου, 4.481, "straight through the shoulder") |
| ἀμφεφόβηθεν (16.290) | "were thrown into panic about" | "were thrown into panic about him" | "fled around", "scattered round", "were terrified round"; ἀμφί + φοβέω, and the note says the sense is taken from the parts |
| ἐν … φόβον ἧκεν (16.291) | "cast terror … among" | "cast terror among them all" | "put fear into", "struck terror", "sent panic"; ἵημι "send, throw"; φόβος "terror" (2.767) |
| ἡμιδαής (16.294) | "half-burnt" | "half-burnt" | "half-consumed", "half-charred", "singed"; ἡμι- "half" + δαίω "burn" |
| ἐπέχυντο (16.295) | "poured themselves … up among" | "poured out among" | "swarmed", "rushed", "spread"; the same verb χέω as ἐξεχέοντο (16.259) and ἐχέοντο (16.267), "poured" |
| στεροπηγερέτα Ζεύς (16.298) | "the lightning-gatherer Zeus" | "Zeus who gathers the lightning" | "lord of lightning" (kept for ἀστεροπητής, "who flashes lightning", 1.580), "the lightning-hurler", "who masses the lightning"; built like νεφεληγερέτα "cloud-gatherer" / "who gathers the clouds" (1.517), στεροπή "lightning" + ἀγείρω "gather" |
| ἐρωή (πολέμου … ἐρωή, 16.302) | "respite" | "respite" | "force", "rush" (the table’s ἐρωή of a shaft or spear, 4.542, 11.357), "pause", "ceasing"; the sense is from the context and the note says so |
| τυτθὸν ἀνέπνευσαν (16.302) | "breathed again a little" | "drew breath again for a little while" | "rested a little", "recovered"; ἀναπνέω "draw breath again" (11.326) |
| προτροπάδην (16.304) | "headlong" | "headlong" | "in rout", "in full flight", "straight on"; an adverb |
| ἀνθίσταντο · ὑπόεικον (16.305) | "stood against" · "gave way" | "stood their ground against" · "gave way" | "resisted", "withstood"; ὑπείκω "give way" (ὑπόεικε, 11.204, "give way") |
| Follows the table unchanged | | | μητίετα Ζεύς and τοῦ δ’ ἔκλυε (Odyssey 20.102), ὣς ἔφατ’ εὐχόμενος (prayer-closing, 3.385), Διὶ πατρί "father Zeus" (3.350), ὄτρυνε μένος καὶ θυμὸν ἑκάστου (5.470, 13.155), ἄλκιμον ἦτορ "a sturdy heart" (16.209), ἐκέκλετο μακρὸν ἀΰσας "gave orders … shouting loudly" (6.66), εὐρύοπα Ζεῦ "far-thundering" / "who thunders from afar", αἴθοπα οἶνον (4.259), θούριδος ἀλκῆς (4.234), ἀρηΐφιλοι Ἀχαιοί "dear to Ares" (6.73, shipped), μῶλον Ἄρηος "the toil of battle" (2.401), ἀγών "gathering-place" (8.200), ἄαπτοι "invincible", ἱπποκορυσταί "armed with horses" (2.1), ὑπερράγη · ἄσπετος αἰθήρ · σκοπιαί · πρώονες · νάπαι (8.557–558), θεσπεσίῳ ὁμάδῳ (13.797), ὅμαδος ἀλίαστος (12.471), δήϊον πῦρ "hostile fire" (2.415), μέγα φρονέοντες (8.553), ἀργυρόπεζα Θέτις (24.92), μεγαλήτωρ "great-spirited" (9.109), κραδίην καὶ θυμόν (2.171). Lines repeated from published parts (16.210, 16.215, 16.238, 16.273–274, 16.216–217 with the final -ν dropped, 16.277, 16.283, 16.296, 16.299) take the published English; no departure from any Odyssey English. |
